OlympiadBench consists of Olympiad-level bilingual (English and Chinese) multimodal scientific problems that require advanced reasoning and problem-solving skills. The benchmark aims to promote the development of AGI systems that can demonstrate human-level performance on these complex, real-world tasks.

OlympiadBench is designed to be a very challenging set of problems, based on the types of questions asked in international science and mathematics Olympiads. These are high-level competitions that test the problem-solving abilities of the world's brightest students.

The problems in OlympiadBench are designed to be challenging, covering a wide range of topics in fields such as physics, mathematics, chemistry, and biology. These problems often involve interpreting and integrating information from multiple modalities, including text, diagrams, formulas, and equations.

description: Breakthrough models AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 solve advanced reasoning problems in mathematics
snippets: Today, we present AlphaProof, a new reinforcement-learning based system for formal math reasoning, and AlphaGeometry 2, an improved version of our geometry-solving system. Together, these systems solved four out of six problems from this year’s International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO), achieving the same level as a silver medalist in the competition for the first time.

More recently, the annual IMO competition has also become widely recognised as a grand challenge in machine learning and an aspirational benchmark for measuring an AI system’s advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

Our solutions were scored according to the IMO’s point-awarding rules by prominent mathematicians Prof Sir Timothy Gowers, an IMO gold medalist and Fields Medal winner, and Dr Joseph Myers, a two-time IMO gold medalist and Chair of the IMO 2024 Problem Selection Committee.
Artificial general intelligence (AGI) with advanced mathematical reasoning has the potential to unlock new frontiers in science and technology.
